statement: Each equation below has exactly one real solution x. For how many of the five equations is that solution a fraction p/q, where p and q are whole numbers? 4^x = 8, 8^x = 4, 2^x = 3, 9^x = 27, 6^x = 24.

choices.misconception: I looked only for whole-number solutions, and none of the five equations has one, so I counted none.
I solved 4^x = 8 and 8^x = 4 by writing everything as powers of 2, but did not notice that 9 and 27 are both powers of 3.
I saw that 6^x = 24 needs x a little less than 2 and guessed x = 7/4 without checking, but 6^(7/4) is only about 23, not 24.
I thought every equation like these must have a fraction as its solution, because any real number can be written as one.

hints: Write both sides of each equation as powers of the same prime where you can.
4^x = 8 becomes 2^(2x) = 2^3, and 9^x = 27 works the same way with 3. For 2^x = 3, suppose x = p/q and raise both sides to the power q. What goes wrong?
If 2^(p/q) = 3 then 2^p = 3^q, but the left side is even and the right side is odd. For 6^x = 24, x = p/q gives 2^p x 3^p = 2^(3q) x 3^q, so p = 3q and p = q at once.

solutions.reliable: Three equations can be solved directly. 4^x = 8 is 2^(2x) = 2^3, so x = 3/2. 8^x = 4 is 2^(3x) = 2^2, so x = 2/3. 9^x = 27 is 3^(2x) = 3^3, so x = 3/2. For 2^x = 3, the solution is between 1 and 2, so it is positive. Suppose it were a fraction p/q with p and q positive whole numbers. Raising 2^(p/q) = 3 to the power q gives 2^p = 3^q, but 2^p is even and 3^q is odd, a contradiction. For 6^x = 24, the solution is again positive, and x = p/q would give 6^p = 24^q, that is 2^p x 3^p = 2^(3q) x 3^q. Each prime must appear to the same power on both sides, so p = 3q and p = q, which forces q = 0, another contradiction. So exactly 3 of the solutions are fractions. The transferable idea: to show a number is not a fraction, assume it is p/q, clear the fraction, and find a clash such as even equals odd.
solutions.elegant: An equation a^x = b with whole numbers a and b has a fraction solution exactly when a and b are powers of one common number, because a^p = b^q forces the same primes, in the same proportions, on both sides. 4 and 8, 8 and 4, 9 and 27 pass this test, while 2 and 3, and 6 and 24, fail it: 3 answers.

whyOnTest: Proving that a number is not a fraction is the classic proof by contradiction: assume x = p/q, clear the denominator and reach a clash, here even against odd or two different powers of the same prime.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
